CA.name: Field horsetail
CA.citation: NC Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox; native throughout temperate North America. Distinguished from the toxic Equisetum palustre (marsh horsetail); genus contains the toxic alkaloid palustrine, a documented commercial adulteration risk (Saslis-Lagoudakis et al. 2015, Scientific Reports)

DE.name: Ackerschachtelhalm
DE.citation: HMPC/EMA herbal monograph reference (via awl.ch); University of Ulm botanical garden. Explicitly and repeatedly distinguished in German sources from the toxic Sumpfschachtelhalm (E. palustre)

FR.name: Prele des champs
FR.citation: French Wikipedia; Florealpes botanical database. Clearly distinguished from prele des marais (E. palustre) and grande prele (E. telmateia)

RU.name: Хвощ полевой
RU.citation: Plantarium.ru; Moscow State University herbarium database (plant.depo.msu.ru); AgroAtlas Russia

US.name: Field horsetail
US.citation: NC Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox; PFAF. Also documented as common horsetail, scouring rush, horsetail; contains thiaminase, a genuine safety consideration with extended use
